label: rem:fermion-boson-chart-localization
title: Fermion--boson sectors as chart-glue data of $\mathbb{P}_q(V)$
html:
The fermion--boson decomposition provides a geometric reading on the quantum projective line. Bosons are horizontal (\alpha_V = 0). Fermions carry non-trivial vertical projections.

By the spectral--chart correspondence, the symmetric and antisymmetric eigenspaces S^2 V \oplus \Lambda^2 V of the braiding c_{V,V} form the spectral data. This pins the chart-transition coefficient of \mathbb{P}_q(V) to \kappa = q^{-1}. The bosonic sector occupies S^2 V with eigenvalue \lambda_+ = q. This classical channel degenerates to \mathbb{P}(V) at q = 1. The fermionic sector occupies the unit summand \Lambda^2 V \cong \mathbf{1} with eigenvalue \lambda_- = -q^{-1}. The chart-glue concentrates here.

We identify \kappa = q^{-1} = \lambda_+^{-1} = -\lambda_- as the parameter determined by the antisymmetric channel. The parameter q measures surviving vertical (fermionic) content between charts. At q = 1, we recover \kappa = 1, decoupling the sectors into the classical inversion z \cdot w = 1. When q \neq 1, geometry deforms the glue, linking fermionic content to the substrate parameter via the Hecke data of c_{V,V} on V \otimes V. This is the geometric action from observation fermion action. The chart-transition carries the fermionic backreaction of an observation.
